job.title: Technical Services Manager
job.description:
Technical Services Manager – Leading FM Provider – Mayfair - 85k + Package

Would you like to work for one of the leading maintenance providers in London? 

Have you got a proven track record with the technical facilities and maintenance services industry?

If so please read on...

An excellent opportunity has arisen to join one of the UK's leading companies in the facilities industry.

They currently maintain a number of facilities and maintenance contracts across the UK and are looking for a Technical Services Manager to work in a brand new high profile building based in Mayfair. 

The main purpose of the job will be to ensure that technical operations within the building are maintained to a very high standard. 

The role will also be responsible for managing the maintenance shift team on site and also dealing with external subcontractors. The role will be supported by a site admin and also a team of four multi skilled shift engineers.

The technical manager will also need to maintain the site's PPMs to 100% completion at a high quality level, ensure compliance and health and safety are conducted to a high standard and also make sure the asset register is updated on a routine basis.

Other on site duties will also include:
  • Manage all technical issues across the buildings.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s H&S and environmental performance on each site.
  • Plan and implement building shutdowns and basic client project works.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s quality procedures on each site.
  • Recruitment of any new staff required on sites.
  • Responsible for the technical development of all staff, which will include annual appraisals.
  • Management of client relationships on a daily basis.
  • Management of all reports.
  • Manage any additional business opportunities that will deliver client satisfaction and increase contract sales revenue.
  • Responsible for the permit system.
Applicants for this role must be able to demonstrate the following:
  • Qualified in electrical or mechanical engineering discipline; C&G, HNC, HND or higher.
  • Strong understanding of building management systems.
  • Strong technical engineering understanding.
  • Previous HV experience.
  • Previous experience of managing engineering teams.
  • Experience of service delivery in high profile financial offices or critical data centres.
  • Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with all levels of staff and clients.

job.title: Technical Service Manager
job.description:
Technical Service Manager - Electrical - Fife - Salary up to £55,000 plus allowances

CBW is recruiting an experienced Technical Services Manager – Electrical to lead the delivery of electrical and hard facilities services within a complex healthcare environment in Fife.

This is a key leadership role, offering the opportunity to oversee critical electrical infrastructure, lead engineering teams and ensure the safe, compliant and efficient operation of essential building services.

You will take responsibility for the delivery of planned preventative maintenance, reactive maintenance and lifecycle replacement programmes, ensuring contractual obligations, Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are consistently achieved.

Working closely with clients, operational teams, contractors and other stakeholders, you will combine strong technical expertise with effective people management, commercial awareness and a proactive approach to service delivery.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead and develop electrical engineering teams, ensuring safe, efficient and high-quality service delivery.

  • Oversee the maintenance and reliability of critical electrical infrastructure, including High Voltage (HV) and Low Voltage (LV) systems.

  • Manage planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive maintenance and lifecycle replacement programmes.

  • Ensure all maintenance activities are completed within agreed timescales and accurately documented.

  • Manage CAFM systems, including work allocation, asset records, maintenance schedules and performance reporting.

  • Ensure compliance with Safe Systems of Work, Permit to Work procedures and relevant statutory requirements.

  • Oversee Authorised Persons (APs) and Competent Persons (CPs), ensuring technical appointments, competencies and responsibilities are maintained.

  • Coordinate additional works, lifecycle projects and the procurement of equipment and materials.

  • Manage external contractors and supply chain partners, monitoring performance, quality, safety and compliance.

  • Promote a strong Health, Safety and Environmental culture through inspections, risk assessments and proactive management.

  • Maintain accurate statutory, technical and contractual documentation, ensuring audit readiness.

  • Lead and support internal and external audits, ensuring corrective actions are implemented promptly.

  • Build effective relationships with clients and stakeholders, providing regular performance updates and attending contract meetings.

  • Manage team performance, including appraisals, training, development plans and competency records.

  • Work closely with the central Service Desk to coordinate resources and maintain operational continuity.

  • Ensure operational procedures, local operating procedures (LOPs) and technical documentation remain compliant with legislation and industry best practice.

  • Prepare contract performance, energy management and operational reports.

  • Monitor budgets, expenditure and financial forecasts, ensuring effective commercial control.

  • Participate in an out-of-hours and on-call management rota as required.

  • Support the organisation's commitment to ethical standards, equality, diversity and inclusion.

Essential Requirements:
  • HNC/HND in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent discipline.

  • Recognised electrical qualifications and/or fully qualified electrician status.

  • Minimum of five years' post-qualification experience in a comparable technical services or contract management role.

  • Proven experience managing electrical and hard services within a contractual facilities management environment.

  • Strong leadership skills, with experience managing and developing engineering teams.

  • Excellent communication, organisation and stakeholder management skills.

  • Demonstrable commercial and financial management experience.

  • Good working knowledge of Microsoft Word, Excel and CAFM systems.

  • Full UK driving licence.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain the required Disclosure Scotland/PVG clearance.

Desirable Experience:
  • Previous experience within healthcare facilities management or a similarly critical environment.

  • Knowledge of healthcare technical standards, including SHTM 06-01, SHTM 06-02 and SHTM 06-03.

  • Experience or certification as an LV and/or HV Authorised or Approved Person.

  • Knowledge of confined spaces, fire safety and lift management.

  • Experience managing projects and delivering engineering works within a live operational environment.

Salary & Benefits: The successful candidate will benefit from a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • 25 days' annual leave plus public holidays.

  • Life assurance worth twice your annual salary.

  • Employee discounts across a wide range of major retailers and brands.

  • Discounted gym membership.

  • Cycle to Work scheme.

  • Holiday purchase scheme.

CBW are currently recruiting for an experienced Resident Liaison Officer to join a leading Renewables team based in Inverness.

The role is focused on ensuring residents are kept fully informed, supported and engaged before, during and after works take place. The successful candidate will build strong relationships with residents, respond to queries and concerns, coordinate information with project teams, and help minimise disruption associated with construction activities.

This is a Inverness based position with regular travel throughout the north of Scotland, reflecting the geographical spread of current and future projects.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the principal contact for residents throughout the lifecycle of works.
  • Provide clear, accurate and timely information regarding planned works, programme dates, access requirements, progress and completion.
  • Build positive and professional relationships with residents, maintaining trust and confidence throughout the project.
  • Identify resident concerns at an early stage and ensure appropriate action is taken.
  • Communicate changes to programmes, working arrangements or planned activities promptly.
  • Ensure residents understand what to expect before, during and following works to their property or communal areas.
  • Undertake regular visits to properties and residential areas affected by project activities.
  • Engage directly with residents to understand their experience and identify any issues requiring attention.
  • Record and follow up resident queries, requests and concerns through to resolution.
  • Identify individual circumstances or additional support requirements and ensure these are communicated to the appropriate members of the project team.
  • Arrange and participate in resident information meetings, briefings and engagement sessions.
  • Prepare and distribute relevant project information and updates.
  • Support residents in understanding project schedules, key milestones and expected completion dates.
  • Receive and manage resident complaints and concerns in a professional and constructive manner.
  • Work with the relevant project, site and management personnel to investigate and resolve issues.
  • Keep residents informed of progress where an issue cannot be resolved immediately.
  • Monitor outstanding matters and ensure appropriate follow-up takes place.
  • Escalate significant, recurring or unresolved issues to the appropriate level of management.
  • Report hazards, incidents, environmental concerns or other matters requiring management attention.
Person Specification:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to establish positive relationships with a wide range of people.
  • A professional, approachable and empathetic manner.
  • Strong listening skills and the ability to understand and respond appropriately to resident concerns.
  • Effective problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple enquiries, priorities and deadlines.
  • Good attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
  • Previous experience in a resident-facing, customer service, community engagement or similar role.
  • Experience within construction, housing, property, facilities management, refurbishment or a related environment would be advantageous.
  • Understanding of the challenges and sensitivities associated with working in occupied residential properties.
  • Experience of handling customer complaints, enquiries or service issues.
  • Familiarity with maintaining electronic records and using digital systems.

Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary up to £35,000 DOE
  • Van and fuel card.
  • Ongoing training and professional development.
  • Career progression within a growing renewable energy business.
  • Company pension.
  • Supportive team environment with a strong focus on quality, safety and continuous improvement.

job.title: Engineering Services Manager
job.description:
Engineering Services Manager – City of London - High profile building  - 80k

Would you like to work for one of the UK's leading service providers, based in one of the most striking buildings on London's skyline?

Are you bored in your current role and looking for a new challenge?

If so, please read on...

An excellent opportunity has arisen to join one of the UK's leading companies in the facilities industry.

They currently maintain a number of hard services maintenance contracts across the UK and are looking for an Engineering Services Manager to work on a high profile, critical building based in the City of London.

The main purpose of the job will be to ensure that technical operations within the building are maintained to a very high standard.

The role will also be responsible for managing the maintenance team on site and also dealing with external subcontractors.  

The Engineering Services Manager will also need to maintain the site's PPM's to 100% completion at a high quality level, ensure compliance and health and safety are conducted to a high standard and also make sure the asset register is updated on a routine basis.

Other on site duties will also include:
  • Manage all technical issues across the building.
  • Manage agreed KPI and SLA’s.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s H&S and environmental performance on site.
  • Plan and implement building shutdowns and basic client project works.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s quality procedures on site.
  • Recruitment of any new staff required on sites.
  • Responsible for the technical development of all staff, which will include annual appraisals.
  • Management of client relationships on a daily basis.
  • Management of all reports.
  • Manage any additional business opportunities that will deliver client satisfaction and increase contract sales revenue.
  • Responsible for the permit system.
Applicants for this role must be able to demonstrate the following:
  • Fully qualified in electrical or mechanical discipline; C&G, HNC, HND or higher.
  • Strong understanding of building management systems.
  • Strong technical engineering understanding.
  • Previous experience of managing large engineering teams.
  • Experience of service delivery in high profile financial offices or critical data centres.
  • Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with all levels of staff and clients.
  • Ability to manage and prioritise a demanding and varying workload.
  • Ability to deliver projects on time and on budget.

job.title: Compliance Supervisor
job.description:
Compliance Supervisor - FM Service Provider - Essex / London - Up to £55,000

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Compliance Supervisor to join an established Facilities Management service provider. The successful candidate will be based out of the client's office in Essex and will be responsible for overseeing and maintaining compliance across a commercial building or portfolio of properties, ensuring that all maintenance activities, contractor works and statutory obligations are carried out in accordance with current legislation, health and safety regulations, company policies and client requirements. The role will focus heavily on the management and review of Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS), Permit to Work systems, compliance audits, statutory documentation and contractor management, ensuring that all activities are undertaken safely, efficiently and to the highest standards. The Compliance Supervisor will work closely with the Engineering Management Team, site engineers, contractors and client representatives to ensure compliance standards are consistently maintained.

Hours of work

Monday to Friday - 08:00am to 17:00pm

Key Duties & Responsibilities

  • Review, assess and approve contractor RAMS prior to works commencing
  • Ensure all RAMS are site-specific, accurate and appropriate for the activities being undertaken
  • Identify potential risks and ensure suitable control measures are implemented
  • Challenge and reject inadequate RAMS, ensuring appropriate amendments are made before authorisation
  • Monitor contractor activities to ensure works are undertaken in accordance with approved RAMS
  • Assist with the preparation and review of internal risk assessments and safe systems of work
  • Oversee the implementation and management of the site's Permit to Work (PTW) system
  • Ensure permits are correctly completed, authorised, monitored and closed out
  • Ensure contractors understand and comply with permit conditions and site safety requirements
  • Conduct regular inspections to verify compliance with the Permit to Work procedures
  • Support the management of statutory and mandatory maintenance compliance across the building or portfolio
  • Ensure planned preventative maintenance (PPM) records, statutory inspections and certification are accurately maintained
  • Monitor compliance relating to electrical systems, fire safety, water hygiene, HVAC systems, lifting equipment and other building services
  • Track outstanding statutory inspections, remedial actions and certification renewals
  • Liaise with engineering teams and specialist contractors to resolve outstanding compliance issues
  • Escalate overdue statutory tasks and significant compliance risks to the Engineering Management Team
  • Support compliance with relevant legislation, including the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act, Electricity at Work Regulations, COSHH and applicable building safety requirements
  • Ensure all contractors complete the required site inductions before commencing work
  • Monitor contractor performance against site health and safety standards
  • Ensure contractors follow agreed procedures, RAMS and permit requirements
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date compliance records, registers and certification
  • Produce weekly and monthly compliance reports for the Engineering Management Team and client.
Requirements

  • Electrically or Mechanically qualified (C&G, NVQ or apprenticeship)
  • Previous experience in a Compliance Supervisor, Compliance Coordinator, Health & Safety Supervisor or similar role within Facilities Management
  • Experience working within a commercial building, critical environment or multi-site FM contract
  • Strong knowledge of RAMS review and Permit to Work procedures
  • Experience conducting compliance audits and contractor inspections
  • Good understanding of statutory compliance requirements within building services maintenance.
  • Experience managing contractors and monitoring health and safety performance
  • Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail
  • Ability to identify compliance risks and implement corrective actions
  • NEBOSH General Certificate or equivalent health and safety qualification (Desirable)
  • IOSH Managing Safely  (Desirable)
  • Experience within a managing agent, property management or hard services FM environment.
  • Happy to attend sites in and around London

job.title: Night Shift Engineer
job.description:
Electrical Night Shift Engineer – 4 on 4 off – Prestigious Commercial Building – Tottenham Court Road, London – £50,000 per annum

CBW Staffing Solutions are currently recruiting for a Night Shift Electrical Engineer to join an established FM service provider at a prestigious commercial building in Tottenham Court Road, London.

The successful candidate will be a fully qualified Electrical Engineer with a strong background in commercial building maintenance. Working as part of a small on-site engineering team, you will be responsible for carrying out planned preventative maintenance (PPM), reactive maintenance, fault-finding and electrical repairs across the site.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established company, offering a competitive salary, a consistent 4 on 4 off night shift pattern, overtime opportunities and further training and career progression.

Package & Hours of Work
  • Salary of up to £50,000 per annum

  • 4 on 4 off shift pattern

  • Night shifts: 20:00 – 08:00

  • Uniform and tools provided

  • Cycle to Work scheme

  • 20 days annual leave

  • Overtime opportunities

  • Company pension scheme

  • Internal progression and development opportunities

Key Duties & Responsibilities
  • Carry out planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and reactive maintenance across all electrical building services.

  • Diagnose faults and undertake electrical fault-finding and repairs.

  • Maintain lighting systems, including lamp and ballast replacements and Simmtronic/Philips lighting systems.

  • Carry out emergency lighting inspections and testing.

  • Maintain electrical distribution systems, including distribution boards and associated equipment.

  • Undertake minor electrical installation works, including installing new sockets, lighting and circuits where appropriately authorised.

  • Ensure all maintenance tasks are completed within agreed timescales and to the required standards.

  • Identify and report faults with building services equipment, taking appropriate action to resolve issues.

  • Ensure all work is completed in accordance with health and safety regulations and site procedures.

  • Escort specialist subcontractors and monitor their activities while on site.

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records and complete all relevant paperwork.

  • Liaise professionally with the client and site management team regarding maintenance issues and service delivery.

  • Ensure contractual obligations, KPIs and SLAs are consistently achieved.

  • Monitor mechanical building services plant and report any faults or abnormalities to the relevant team.

Requirements
  • Electrically qualified to Level 2 and Level 3, such as City & Guilds or NVQ, or equivalent.

  • 18th Edition Wiring Regulations qualification.

  • Proven experience working within commercial building maintenance.

  • Strong knowledge of electrical PPM, reactive maintenance and fault-finding.

  • Experience working within a large commercial building would be advantageous.

  • Must be able to provide copies of relevant electrical qualifications and trade certificates.

  • Good communication and problem-solving skills.

  • Professional, client-facing approach.

  • Reliable and able to work independently during night shifts.

How to Apply If you are a qualified Electrical Engineer looking for your next opportunity in London, please send your CV to Alex Denton at CBW Staffing Solutions to avoid missing out on this opportunity

job.title: Maintenance Manager

Maintenance Manager – Landmark Building – North West London - 65K

Would you like to work at one of the most recognised and established buildings in North West London?

If so please read on...

One of our long standing clients is currently looking to recruit a Maintenance Manager to work as part of their busy estates team to help service and maintain one of their most important contracts based in North West London.   

They are looking for an experienced Maintenance Manager who will be able to provide a first class customer service and be able to organise, manage and motivate their engineering team; as well as supporting the senior management.

The role will also be reporting directly to the  Manager, who you will be working closely with on a day to day basis.

The hours of work are Monday to Friday, 8-5 and the main duties of the role are as follows:
  • Control of all electrical services, together with management of all associated engineering contracts.
  • Manage all statutory compliance.
  • Control of all building services, infrastructure, maintenance and repairs.
  • Assist with project management of any building refurbishment projects.
  • Ensure that all plant, back up and monitoring systems are maintained in good functioning order at all times, including the testing of all essential systems on a regular basis and in accordance with any relevant legislation.
  • Control of trouble-shooting engineering support.
  • Day to day support and adjustment of infrastructure as required, including liaison with user groups, preparation of documentation for changes, approved appointment of contractors and site supervision.
  • Control of all relevant outsourced contracts.
  • Ensure all procedures are adhered to by all relevant contractors and in accordance with current legislation.
  • Ensure frequent checks are carried out to ensure cost effectiveness against market trends and that value for money is realised for all services.
  • Chair regular update meetings with all contract managers relevant to services provided.
  • Management of electrical related ‘incidents/outages’
  • Implement plans and actions through your leadership skill to identify and deliver additional work opportunities and technical solutions
  • Provide technical guidance and support as required to ensure electrical systems are maintained to a high standard and defects are swiftly identified and rectified.
  • Effective co-ordination of available resources to achieve technical and innovative solutions.
  • Lead the team to achieve sustainability objectives to improve energy consumption through operational enhancement, whilst seeking out efficient technologies and scoping proposals for consideration
Applicants for this role must be able to meet the following criteria:
  • Recognised apprenticeship and fully electrical qualified to recognised level ie C&G, HNC/HND.
  • Proven background in a hard services maintenance role. 
  • Previous experience and involvement in managing contractors. 
  • Experience of working within large estate environments.
  • A strong and committed team player capable of prioritising and solving problems often under pressure, utilising innovative solutions.
  • Must be a team player committed to working in a quality and professional environment.
  • Strong people management skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

job.description:

Due to continued growth in the renewable energy sector, we are recruiting experienced professionals to support the delivery of residential and commercial Solar PV and Battery Storage installations across Scotland and the wider UK.

Successful candidates will join dedicated installation teams, working together to deliver high-quality renewable energy systems safely, efficiently, and to industry standards.

job.title: Mechanical Plumber

job.title: Fit Out Supervisor
job.description:

Exciting opportunity to work for an establish Property Manager company based in London. As the Fit-out Supervisor you will be a key experienced member of the property engineering team, carrying out duties as part of tenants and landlord fit-out, as directed by the engineering management team. You will coordinate between the tenant’s project team and M&E consultants. You will supervise a wide range of tasks on Landlord plant and equipment including electrical, mechanical, water treatment, domestic systems, cooling towers and HVAC plant. In return the company is offering a fixed term contract until August 2027, Up to £67,500, + Bonus/Package.

Hours of work

Monday to Friday - 08:00am to 17:30pm

Key duties & Responsibilities

  • Review contractor and tenant RAMS, issue and control permits to work.
  • Review and monitor access into landlord areas and plantrooms.
  • Maintain effective communication with the appointed fit out coordinator and M&E consultants.
  • Attend fit out meetings with the tenants, their contractors and fit out coordinator.
  • Monitor the tenant’s fit-out project, identifying any potential impacts to the base build infrastructure.
  • Undertake and supervise tasks as directed by the engineering management team and provide assistance to fit out coordinator, ensuring all work is carried out to required codes of practices and standards.
  • Verify commissioning and any integrations to base build systems, ensuring systems and O&M are updated.
  • Ensure the CAFM system is updated with sufficient information following any reactive tasks.
  • Carry out fault finding, diagnostics and rectification on HVAC systems, escalating where necessary.

  • Plant areas, workshops, stores and changing areas are kept to the highest standards of housekeeping.
  • Supervision and monitoring of contractors carrying out work and or fit out contractors.
  • Always uphold the integrity of the company and ensure the provision of high levels of customer services are provided.
  • Maintain effective reporting including critical plant status, plant isolations, issues arising, ongoing works, special task requests, and standard of housekeeping.
  • Ensure the accurate and timely completion of logbooks on completion of any related activities.
  • Ensure that specialist contractor service reports are signed off where necessary, that quality of work has been inspected, and faults/recommendations are escalated to the management team.
  • Escalate any defects and incidents immediately to engineering management.
  • Complete any site-specific system training as directed by your line manager.

  • Operation, diagnostics and fault finding for the following: HVAC plant – Pumps, motors, actuators, air handling units, pipework,fixtures and fittings, Public health systems and equipment – Taps, WHB, TMV’s, water
  • heaters, domestic hot and cold water, drainage systems, Boilers and Heating systems, Water treatment plant incl. cooling towers, Building Management and Energy Management Systems and Electrical systems and equipment.

Requirements
  • C&G, Level 3 or similar qualifications in electrical, mechanical or plumbing and heating.

  • Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)

  • Initiative to suggest and develop new ideas to increase efficiency and cost savings.
  • Ability to prioritise tasks to meet deadlines
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to deal with staff at all levels
  • Experience of supervising large engineering teams and or fit out teams
  • Able to commit to the FTC (August 2027)

Desirable

  • Experience of system modifications and minor installations

  • Awareness of the Tenant and landlord relationship within multi-occupied properties
  • Understanding of energy management systems and energy reduction initiatives
  • PASMA and IPAF qualifications
  • First aid training
  • Authorised Person in Electrical or Mechanical discipline

Site Manager - Glasgow - Salary up to £45,000 Plus company vehicle

We’re currently recruiting for an experienced Site Manager to join a growing team delivering Smart Home and Renewable Energy projects across Scotland.

As Site Manager, you’ll take responsibility for the successful day-to-day delivery of projects, ensuring work is completed safely, on programme, within budget and to a high standard.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Managing site operations, subcontractors and installation teams.
  • Providing leadership and ensuring high standards of workmanship and customer service.
  • Coordinating with senior management, procurement and supply chain teams to ensure projects are properly planned and resourced.
  • Supporting the delivery of renewable energy installations, including Solar PV and Air Source Heat Pumps, with an understanding of whole-house retrofit.
  • Ensuring compliance with Health & Safety, RAMS, Toolbox Talks and relevant legislation, including PAS 2030 and PAS 2035.
  • Monitoring project programmes, progress, costs and quality.
  • Producing regular project reports and chairing site meetings.
  • Managing customer queries and resolving issues efficiently.
  • Ensuring quality, environmental and health & safety procedures are followed and accurately recorded.
  • Keeping up to date with relevant industry regulations, HSE, Ofgem and retrofit requirements.
Person Specification:
  • Previous experience within renewable energy construction, retrofit or residential installation (Desirable)
  • Experience managing subcontractors and installation teams
  • Strong organisational and problem-solving skills
  • SMSTS
  • First Aid
  • Full UK driving licence
  • Good understanding of Health & Safety and site compliance
  • Flexibility to travel and stay away from home across Scotland
Salary & Benefits:
  • £45,000 salary
  • Company vehicle – fully expensed
  • 22 days’ holiday + Bank Holidays
  • Overnight allowances when working away from home
  • Bonus scheme
  • Opportunity to work on a variety of renewable energy and smart home projects
  • Long-term opportunity within a growing sector

Technical Account Manager - Trophy Building - Central London - up to 85K

One of the capital's leading service providers is currently looking to recruit a Technical Account Manager to work at a large prestigious building in Central London.  

As a company, they manage properties for a number of well known commercial blue chip clients and are considered one of the best in their field.

The main purpose of the role will be to ensure that all technical and contractual operations in this building are maintained to a very high standard.

There will also be a high level of responsibility with regards to compliance, HV systems and contractor management.    

The main duties will also include:
  • Manage and work alongside the appointed contractors.
  • Manage all technical issues including HV systems and shutdowns.
  • Attend client meetings.
  • Manage agreed KPI and SLA’s.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s H&S and environmental performance on site.
  • Plan and implement building shutdowns and complex client project works.
  • Responsible for managing the company’s quality procedures on site.
  • Recruitment of any new staff required on sites.
  • Responsible for the technical development of all staff, which will include annual appraisals.
  • Management of client relationships on a daily basis.
  • Management of all reports.
  • Manage any additional business opportunities that will deliver client satisfaction and increase contract sales revenue.
  • Responsible for the permit system.
Applicants for this role must be able to demonstrate the following:
  • Qualified in elec/mech engineering discipline; C&G, HNC, HND or higher.
  • Strong understanding of HV systems and ideally HV approved.
  • Strong technical engineering understanding.
  • Previous experience of managing large engineering teams.
  • Experience of managing large 24/7 sites.
  • Experience of service delivery in high profile financial offices.
  • Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with all levels of staff and clients.
  • Ability to manage and prioritise a demanding and varying workload.
  • Ability to deliver projects on time and on budget.
The package for this role includes:
  • Salary up to 85k.
  • 25 days holiday.
  • Pension.
  • Healthcare.

job.title: Tenant Liaison Officer
job.description:
Tenant Liaison Officer - Inverness - Salary up to £35,000 DOE

CBW are currently recruiting for an experienced Resident Liaison Officer to join a leading Renewables team based in Inverness.

The role is focused on ensuring residents are kept fully informed, supported and engaged before, during and after works take place. The successful candidate will build strong relationships with residents, respond to queries and concerns, coordinate information with project teams, and help minimise disruption associated with construction activities.

This is a Inverness based position with regular travel throughout the north of Scotland, reflecting the geographical spread of current and future projects.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the principal contact for residents throughout the lifecycle of works.
  • Provide clear, accurate and timely information regarding planned works, programme dates, access requirements, progress and completion.
  • Build positive and professional relationships with residents, maintaining trust and confidence throughout the project.
  • Identify resident concerns at an early stage and ensure appropriate action is taken.
  • Communicate changes to programmes, working arrangements or planned activities promptly.
  • Ensure residents understand what to expect before, during and following works to their property or communal areas.
  • Undertake regular visits to properties and residential areas affected by project activities.
  • Engage directly with residents to understand their experience and identify any issues requiring attention.
  • Record and follow up resident queries, requests and concerns through to resolution.
  • Identify individual circumstances or additional support requirements and ensure these are communicated to the appropriate members of the project team.
  • Arrange and participate in resident information meetings, briefings and engagement sessions.
  • Prepare and distribute relevant project information and updates.
  • Support residents in understanding project schedules, key milestones and expected completion dates.
  • Receive and manage resident complaints and concerns in a professional and constructive manner.
  • Work with the relevant project, site and management personnel to investigate and resolve issues.
  • Keep residents informed of progress where an issue cannot be resolved immediately.
  • Monitor outstanding matters and ensure appropriate follow-up takes place.
  • Escalate significant, recurring or unresolved issues to the appropriate level of management.
  • Report hazards, incidents, environmental concerns or other matters requiring management attention.
Person Specification:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to establish positive relationships with a wide range of people.
  • A professional, approachable and empathetic manner.
  • Strong listening skills and the ability to understand and respond appropriately to resident concerns.
  • Effective problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple enquiries, priorities and deadlines.
  • Good attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
  • Previous experience in a resident-facing, customer service, community engagement or similar role.
  • Experience within construction, housing, property, facilities management, refurbishment or a related environment would be advantageous.
  • Understanding of the challenges and sensitivities associated with working in occupied residential properties.
  • Experience of handling customer complaints, enquiries or service issues.
  • Familiarity with maintaining electronic records and using digital systems.

Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary up to £35,000 DOE
  • Van and fuel card.
  • Ongoing training and professional development.
  • Career progression within a growing renewable energy business.
  • Company pension.
  • Supportive team environment with a strong focus on quality, safety and continuous improvement.

job.title: Resident Liaison Officer
job.description:
Resident Liaison Officer - Inverness - Salary up to £30,000 DOE

CBW are currently recruiting for an experienced Resident Liaison Officer to join a leading Renewables team based in Inverness.

The role is focused on ensuring residents are kept fully informed, supported and engaged before, during and after works take place. The successful candidate will build strong relationships with residents, respond to queries and concerns, coordinate information with project teams, and help minimise disruption associated with construction activities.

This is a Inverness - based position with regular travel throughout the north of Scotland, reflecting the geographical spread of current and future projects.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Act as the principal contact for residents throughout the lifecycle of works.
  • Provide clear, accurate and timely information regarding planned works, programme dates, access requirements, progress and completion.
  • Build positive and professional relationships with residents, maintaining trust and confidence throughout the project.
  • Identify resident concerns at an early stage and ensure appropriate action is taken.
  • Communicate changes to programmes, working arrangements or planned activities promptly.
  • Ensure residents understand what to expect before, during and following works to their property or communal areas.
  • Undertake regular visits to properties and residential areas affected by project activities.
  • Engage directly with residents to understand their experience and identify any issues requiring attention.
  • Record and follow up resident queries, requests and concerns through to resolution.
  • Identify individual circumstances or additional support requirements and ensure these are communicated to the appropriate members of the project team.
  • Arrange and participate in resident information meetings, briefings and engagement sessions.
  • Prepare and distribute relevant project information and updates.
  • Support residents in understanding project schedules, key milestones and expected completion dates.
  • Receive and manage resident complaints and concerns in a professional and constructive manner.
  • Work with the relevant project, site and management personnel to investigate and resolve issues.
  • Keep residents informed of progress where an issue cannot be resolved immediately.
  • Monitor outstanding matters and ensure appropriate follow-up takes place.
  • Escalate significant, recurring or unresolved issues to the appropriate level of management.
  • Report hazards, incidents, environmental concerns or other matters requiring management attention.
Person Specification:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to establish positive relationships with a wide range of people.
  • A professional, approachable and empathetic manner.
  • Strong listening skills and the ability to understand and respond appropriately to resident concerns.
  • Effective problem-solving and conflict-resolution skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple enquiries, priorities and deadlines.
  • Good attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
  • Previous experience in a resident-facing, customer service, community engagement or similar role.
  • Experience within construction, housing, property, facilities management, refurbishment or a related environment would be advantageous.
  • Understanding of the challenges and sensitivities associated with working in occupied residential properties.
  • Experience of handling customer complaints, enquiries or service issues.
  • Familiarity with maintaining electronic records and using digital systems.

Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary up to £30,000 DOE
  • Van and fuel card.
  • Ongoing training and professional development.
  • Career progression within a growing renewable energy business.
  • Company pension.
  • Supportive team environment with a strong focus on quality, safety and continuous improvement.

job.title: Soft Services Manager

Soft Services Manager – 9-Month FTC Salary: Up to £50,000
Contract: 9-Month Fixed-Term Contract

Working Pattern: Hybrid

About the role

My client is currently recruiting for a Soft Services Manager to take a key leadership role within a busy and evolving service environment on a 9-month fixed-term contract.

The role will suit someone who is confident working at both strategic and operational level and who can turn ideas and recommendations into practical improvements that deliver measurable results.

 

Main Duties 

  • Lead and support operational managers, creating clear accountability and a positive culture of performance, collaboration and continuous improvement.

  • Build strong and professional relationships with clients, establishing effective communication, review and escalation processes.

  • Take ownership of contract performance, ensuring key information, obligations, variations, additional works and upcoming renewals are properly managed.

  • Review staffing structures, resource deployment, agency usage, overtime, supervision and cover arrangements to identify opportunities for greater efficiency.

  • Develop a clear understanding of productivity across different sites and use operational data to improve working practices and service delivery.

  • Strengthen budget and cost controls, working closely with Finance to understand variances, forecasting and operational expenditure.

  • Identify opportunities to improve value for money through procurement, equipment, consumables, stock management and working practices.

  • Introduce effective inspection, audit and performance management processes to ensure quality and compliance.

  • Work closely with relevant Health & Safety, Quality, HR, Finance and Procurement teams to ensure appropriate standards and controls are maintained.

  • Improve management information and introduce practical digital processes for scheduling, reporting, auditing, action tracking and documentation.

  • Strengthen workforce planning, recruitment, induction, training, attendance, succession planning and resource management.

  • Develop forward plans for key contracts, identifying renewal requirements, commercial risks, pricing considerations and opportunities for service improvement.

  • Contribute to the future development of the Soft Services function and provide evidence-based recommendations to senior leadership.

 

About you 

We are looking for someone with strong operational management experience within soft services, facilities management, cleaning, FM or a similar environment.

You will ideally have:

  • Proven experience managing operational teams and managers.

  • Strong contract and client management experience.

  • A good understanding of workforce planning and resource deployment.

  • Experience managing budgets, costs and commercial performance.

  • A track record of delivering operational improvements and efficiencies.

  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills.

  • Experience working with multiple stakeholders across operational and support functions.

  • Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to turn data into practical actions.

  • Experience of quality assurance, audits, compliance and performance management.

  • Confidence using digital systems and management information to improve operational control.

  • The ability to work independently while also building effective relationships across an organisation.

Most importantly, you'll be a practical, proactive and credible leader who can engage people, challenge existing ways of working and make improvements happen.

 

Why join?

This is an opportunity to make a real impact during a focused 9-month fixed-term assignment, helping to strengthen operational performance and shape the future direction of Soft Services.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Make a genuine impact on service performance and operational efficiency.

  • Lead and develop operational managers and teams.

  • Influence how Soft Services are delivered in the future.

  • Work closely with senior leaders and a range of professional functions.

  • Develop and implement new processes, systems and ways of working.

  • Build strong client relationships and influence service outcomes.

  • Work in a hybrid role based in Greenwich, London.

  • Earn a salary of up to £50,000, depending on experience.

Interested?

If you're an experienced Soft Services or Facilities Management professional looking for a 9-month fixed-term opportunity where you can make a tangible difference, we'd be keen to hear from you.

If you enjoy leading people, improving services and delivering measurable operational results, this could be an excellent next step for you.

 

If you would like to apply for this position please contact claire@cbwstaffingsolutions.com

We are seeking an experienced Electrical Compliance Supervisor to join a growing renewable energy business delivering a high volume of domestic energy installations across Scotland.

This is a hands-on technical and supervisory position, responsible for maintaining consistently high standards of electrical quality, compliance and safety across a busy installation programme. You will work closely with a small team of Compliance Inspectors, installation teams and site management, carrying out both remote and on-site inspections across Solar PV, battery storage, Air Source Heat Pumps (ASHP) and Electrical Storage Heating installations.

The role offers a genuine mix of technical, field and office-based responsibilities, including reviewing electrical certification and photographic evidence, supporting installers with technical queries, identifying quality issues and providing coaching and training to installation and inspection teams.

There is also the opportunity for the successful candidate to become, or work towards becoming, a NICEIC Qualifying Supervisor.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead and support a team of Compliance Inspectors, ensuring inspection activity keeps pace with a high-volume installation programme.
  • Carry out remote and on-site inspections, reviewing workmanship, materials, installation methods and supporting documentation.
  • Apply strong practical electrical knowledge to assess the installation, wiring, configuration and commissioning of inverters and battery storage systems.
  • Identify and troubleshoot electrical and system faults both remotely and on-site.
  • Provide technical support to installation teams, inspectors and customers, acting as a key point of contact for electrical and system-related queries.
  • Support the training and development of site and office-based colleagues, enabling effective first-line fault diagnosis and technical triage.
  • Liaise with manufacturers and equipment suppliers to resolve technical issues, faults and warranty matters.
  • Monitor installation quality and identify examples of best and poor practice, feeding learning into toolbox talks, training and best-practice guidance.
  • Deliver technical updates, toolbox talks and product awareness sessions to installation and inspection teams.
  • Review photographic evidence and job documentation to ensure installations can be effectively inspected remotely.
  • Ensure electrical installation work meets relevant engineering specifications, BS 7671, NICEIC requirements, MCS standards and applicable health, safety and environmental requirements.
  • Review electrical certificates, including EICs, Minor Works Certificates and EICRs, for accuracy and compliance.
  • Ensure project documentation is complete and meets relevant renewable energy certification requirements before sign-off.
  • Support internal and external quality, compliance and regulatory audits.
Person Specification: You will be an experienced electrical professional with a strong understanding of renewable energy installations and a genuine interest in maintaining high standards of workmanship and compliance.

  • A strong electrical installation background with relevant industry experience.
  • Practical knowledge of Solar PV, battery storage and associated inverter systems.
  • Experience of electrical inspection, testing and fault finding.
  • Good working knowledge of BS 7671.
  • Understanding of MCS requirements and renewable energy compliance.
  • Experience reviewing electrical certification and installation documentation.
  • The ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues both remotely and on-site.
  • NICEIC Qualifying Supervisor experience or an individual working towards this level would be highly desirable.
Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary up to £50,000 DOE
  • Company vehicle and fuel card.
  • Ongoing training and professional development.
  • Career progression within a growing renewable energy business.
  • Company pension.
  • Consistent workload across Solar PV, Battery Storage, EV Charging and Heat Pump projects.
  • Supportive team environment with a strong focus on quality, safety and continuous improvement.
